name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 23 points Republican, among the reddest House seats
Crawford holds roughly $1 million on hand versus about $12,000 for Green
Prediction markets price Crawford near 97 percent to win
No public polling; the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Crawford's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial advantage over Terri Green leave the Democrat with no realistic path; market pricing and fundamentals point the same way toward a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: A historically strong Democratic midterm wave or heavy late outside spending could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arkansas's 1st District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and six-term incumbent Rick Crawford is seeking another term after easily clearing renomination. The district's partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward Republicans sets a high bar for any challenger, and even a favorable 2026 midterm environment would need to be historically extreme to put the seat in play.

Democrat Terri Green has raised about $65,000 and had roughly $12,000 on hand, while Crawford has raised more than $940,000 with about $1 million banked. No public polls of the race are available, and prediction markets price Crawford's chances at about 97 percent. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot but is not viewed as a factor. Everything points to Crawford winning another term comfortably.
